data.name: Narayan
data.gender_notes: Narayan is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who possesses the supreme power and is the ruler of the universe. The name Narayan carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Narayan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the supreme form of God, Vishnu, who is the preserver of the universe
data.etymology: Narayan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narayan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Narayan is a popular name among Hindus and is also known as Vishnu or Hari. The name is often used interchangeably to refer to the supreme god of the Hindu trinity- Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. The name is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, with numerous temples, hymns, and scriptures dedicated to this deity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, Narayan represents the cosmic aspect of Vishnu who lies in an eternal repose on the serene waters of the cosmic ocean. He is the divine force that sustains and protects the universe. The name signifies the ultimate reality and the source of all creation. Devotion to Narayan is believed to lead to spiritual growth and liberation from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Narayan is a Sanskrit name meaning "resting place of the divine". It is a name for Vishnu, denoting his role as the supreme cosmic power, the eternal rest and refuge for all souls.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Narayan continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Narayan from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of Narayan - "Lord of the Universe". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
